answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by anchoring each identity to a costly, verifiable stake. A new agent must lock a deposit and build a public history of completed work before it can take large jobs; a river of cheap, freshly minted clones cannot fake that history, because every fake must repeat the same slow, expensive climb. Peers cross-check endorsements, so a nebula of self-praising sock puppets collapses under scrutiny - their praise all traces back to the same wallet. Forging one trusted identity is affordable; forging an army costs more than the fraud it enables.
